title: Sabalenka opens China Open with victory and discusses self-pressure
summary:
Aryna Sabalenka began her China Open campaign by beating Mexico's Renata Zarazua. After the match, she discussed her efforts to be easier on herself while dealing with high expectations.

The world number two won 6-1, 6-3 in 63 minutes. She hit 11 aces and did not face a break point. An ace is a legal serve that the receiver does not touch. A break point gives the receiver a chance to win a game on the opponent's serve.

This was Sabalenka's first match since losing her world number one ranking and her US Open crown to Elena Rybakina in September. She was seeking her first title since March, when she won Indian Wells and the Miami Open back-to-back. That pair of victories is known as the Sunshine Double.

Sabalenka explained that demanding more from herself has both helpful and difficult effects. Sometimes those expectations push her forward, she said, but sometimes they drain her energy.

She said: "I'm really trying so hard sometimes to be easier on myself."

Her comments describe how she experiences pressure in her own tennis career. She said learning to be less self-critical was something she still needed to work on.

Sabalenka was set to face Czech player Nikola Bartunkova in the third round. Bartunkova had come close to beating her at the Berlin Open in June. The China Open victory gave Sabalenka a winning start as she continued her search for another tournament title.
why_it_matters: Sabalenka's account explains how high expectations can both motivate an athlete and take energy, alongside a concrete tournament result.
